timeline.text: Hello. I can see you are in the main Settings menu. I want to turn your iPhone into a bedside clock using the StandBy feature. First, let's go into the StandBy settings and turn it on. How can I get you there?
I see you tapped on Control Center. That's not where we are going. Let's go back to the main Settings list and tap on StandBy.
Good. You're finally in the right place. Tap on 'Always On' to turn it off so the screen won't glow all night.

Wait! You accidentally turned off Night Mode too. I asked you to turn off 'Always On' so the screen doesn't glow, but I told you to *keep* Night Mode on. Tap the 'Night Mode' switch again to turn it back ON.
tap Night Mode ; tap Always On
Good. Now under 'Notifications', you see 'Show Notifications' is still ON. Tap that switch to turn it off so it doesn't show alerts on the screen.

From the iPhone User Guide — “Use StandBy to view information at a distance while iPhone is charging”:

You can use StandBy to turn your iPhone into a bedside clock, a photo frame, a display for viewing widgets or Live Activities in full screen, and more.

Start StandBy
1. Go to Settings > StandBy and make sure StandBy is turned on.
2. Connect iPhone to a charger and set it down on its side, keeping it stationary.
3. Press the side button.
4. Swipe left or right to switch between widgets, photos, and clocks. Swipe up or down to scroll between options for each of these views. When Night Mode is turned on for StandBy, the screen adapts to low ambient light at night and displays items with a red tint so that it’s not intrusive while you’re sleeping.

With the Always-On display (on supported models ), StandBy stays on to show useful information. For all other iPhone models, it’s easy to activate StandBy any time by either tapping the screen, gently nudging the table your iPhone is on, or using Siri.

In each location where you charge iPhone with MagSafe, StandBy remembers your preferred view, whether that’s a clock, photos, or widgets. For example, you can have it set up for family photos in the kitchen or an alarm clock at your bedside.

Set display preferences for when StandBy is on

1. Go to Settings > StandBy > Display.
2. Choose one of the following: Automatically: The display turns off when iPhone isn’t in use and the room is dark. After 20 Seconds: The display turns off after 20 seconds. Never: The display stays on as long as StandBy is on.

== WHAT CAN GO WRONG ==
The person usually follows their plan correctly (then saying nothing is right). But they can make a real mistake — the kinds you know:
  wrong_value: picks the WRONG option or value for a control the task set (the wrong payee, 'Ask' instead of 'Never')
  wrong_target: actuates a NEIGHBOURING control instead of the intended one, leaving the intended one untouched
  wrong_page: takes a wrong turn and ends up on a page that is not on the way to the task
  extra_write: changes a setting the task said to leave alone, or that it never asked for
They may also ask you a question (answer briefly and correctly), or ANNOUNCE a change of plan out loud. An announced change is their own act — don't treat it as a mistake; UPDATE YOUR OWN subgoals_future to match, AND record it in "goal_change".
